name: TLV75533PDBVR
title: TLV755P: 500 mA low-IQ low-dropout regulator with fixed output, enable and active discharge
summary: A family of fixed-output PMOS linear regulators supplying up to 500 mA from 1.45 V to 5.5 V on 25 µA typical ground current. Outputs from 0.6 V to 5 V, accuracy within 1 % to 85 °C in DBV and DRV, built-in soft-start, foldback current limit, thermal shutdown, UVLO and a 120 Ω output pulldown when disabled. Stable on a 1 µF ceramic output capacitor. Comes in SOT-23-5 (DBV), SOT-23-5 with thermal pad (DYD), X2SON-4 (DQN) and WSON-6 (DRV); TLV75533PDBVR is the 3.3 V part in SOT-23-5 on a 3000-piece reel.

circuits.title: Post-regulator after a DC/DC converter
circuits.description: A 3.3 V TLV755P runs from the 4.3 V output of a switching converter and supplies a 250 mA DC load at up to 70 °C ambient, with input current up to 500 mA. A 1 µF capacitor sits across the converter output at IN and another across the load at OUT. EN is the on/off control.

circuits.title: Reverse current protection with a Schottky diode
circuits.description: A Schottky diode from OUT (anode) to IN (cathode) lies in parallel with the pass transistor's internal body diode. When the output would rise above the input, the Schottky carries the reverse current instead of the regulator. CIN and COUT sit from IN and OUT to ground.

operation.text: A PMOS-pass linear regulator with fixed outputs from 0.6 V to 5 V, running from 1.45 V to 5.5 V and delivering up to 500 mA on about 25 µA of quiescent current. It has enable, soft-start, foldback current limit, undervoltage lockout, thermal shutdown and an active output pulldown. Junction operating range is –40 °C to +125 °C.

A bandgap reference drives the error amplifier, which compares it with the output through an internal divider (lower resistor R2 = 550 kΩ, upper resistor R1 set per output voltage). Current limit, thermal shutdown and UVLO act on the pass device, and logic switches a 120 Ω resistor from OUT to GND when the part is off.
Until VIN rises past VUVLO (1.3 V typical, 1.21 V to 1.44 V) the output stays off and is held to ground through the 120 Ω pulldown. Hysteresis is 40 mV typical.

EN is active high: above VHI (1 V min) the regulator runs, below VLO (0.3 V max) it shuts down. Where no shutdown is wanted EN is tied to IN. When disabled, the 120 Ω pulldown discharges the output with the time constant of COUT against 120 Ω in parallel with the load. EN works independently of IN, but driven above VIN it draws more current; sequencing EN after VIN or tying EN to IN avoids that, and with EN above VIN its toggle rate stays below 10 kHz.
An internal soft-start ramps the output monotonically at turn-on, limiting inrush current and the dip it would cause on the input. Start-up time is 550 µs typical.

The limit is a fixed current (ICL, 560 mA to 865 mA) until the output falls below 0.4 × VOUT(NOM); below that the allowed current is scaled back as the output approaches ground, reaching ISC (355 mA typical) into a short. In limit the output is unregulated and equals the limited current times the load resistance. A sustained short heats the pass device with (VIN – VOUT) × ISC until thermal shutdown; it restarts once cool, and cycles between limit and shutdown while the fault lasts. During start-up the foldback holds current below ICL, so a constant-current load, or an output negative at enable, can keep the output from reaching its nominal value; such a load is held off until the output is up. Excess inductance in the output path makes the limit oscillate under a fault and is kept small.

The output turns off at about 165 °C junction and back on at about 155 °C, so under heavy dissipation the part cycles. Normal operation keeps TJ at or below 125 °C; repeated thermal shutdown shortens the part's life. Margin is checked by raising ambient temperature with worst-case load until the protection trips.

Normal: VIN above VOUT(NOM) + VDO, EN has risen past its rising threshold and not fallen below its falling one, IOUT below ICL and TJ below TSD. Dropout: everything else normal but VIN below VOUT(NOM) + VDO; the output follows the input, the pass transistor is in triode, and line or load steps cause large output swings. Coming out of a steady dropout state (not at start-up) the loop has driven the pass device fully on, so VOUT overshoots VOUT(NOM) on fast transients while regulation returns. Disabled: EN below VLO, VIN below VUVLO or TJ above TSD; the pass device is off, internal circuits shut down and the output is pulled to ground, the pulldown working while enough input voltage is present.

Stability needs 0.47 µF or more of effective output capacitance; with the 50 % derating assumed for ceramics, 1 µF nominal is placed on both IN and OUT. X5R and X7R ceramics are used for their small change in value and ESR over temperature; DC-bias loss grows with output voltage. For best performance the output capacitance stays at or below 200 µF. The input capacitor lowers the source impedance, helps transient response and PSRR, and counters a reactive source; a source with high impedance over a wide band gets several input capacitors in parallel, and a larger one is used for big fast load steps or when the source is several inches away.

Below the dropout voltage the PMOS pass transistor is in its linear region and the input-to-output path is its RDS(ON), so VDO rises in proportion to output current. PSRR and transient response worsen as VIN – VOUT nears dropout.

A slow input ramp at start-up can put the regulator in dropout, and the output overshoots when it regains regulation; enabling the part with EN after the input is up avoids this. A line step while in dropout also overshoots, because the error amplifier has pulled the pass gate fully down and must slew the gate back; if that overshoot is too large, more input capacitance slows the step.

Current from OUT back to IN flows through the pass transistor's body diode and, when large, degrades the part through electromigration, heating or latch-up. It arises when a large COUT holds the output up as the input collapses at light load, when the output is driven before the input is present, or when the output is driven above the input; all exceed the VOUT ≤ VIN + 0.3 V rating. Where it is expected, external protection such as a Schottky diode from OUT to IN is used.

Dissipation is set by the input-output difference and load; choosing the input rail close to the output keeps it low. The board area around the regulator is kept clear of other heat sources. On the packages with a thermal pad the pad is the main heat path: it is soldered to a copper area with plated vias to inner or bottom planes. RθJA varies with the board and serves only as a relative comparison; the ψJT and ψJB metrics estimate junction temperature from a measured package-top or board temperature and do not depend much on copper area.
IN is fed from a low-impedance source. A reactive source gets more input capacitance, added alongside the 1 µF part.

CIN and COUT go as close to the part as possible, connections use copper planes for heat, and thermal vias around the part spread it. A thermal pad is soldered to copper; left unsoldered, thermal resistance rises sharply. In the example layouts for DQN, DBV, DRV and DYD, CIN sits at IN, COUT at OUT, and a ground plane runs under the part.
